messages:
aisha: Heads-up — Plainsky wants to POC next week. They asked to validate the 'orch-14b-opt' variant for their orchestration agent. Need: catalog fit, kv-cache/quant compatibility, security questionnaire answers, and a pricing sketch. Can someone triage infra gaps?

tom_se: I can take lead on variant compatibility. Quick Q: are they planning streaming or sync gen?

aisha: Streaming for control-plane signals, but latency-sensitive for short completions (~50 tokens).

tom_se: OK. orch-14b-opt is quant-friendly but depends on KV layout. If they do long context prefixing we'll need KV caching tests.

rina_infra: Re KV: our current compact-kv layout works with orch-14b-opt v1.2, but we hit perf cliffs when sequence + batch combos exceed 2.5k tokens total across requests. Need to validate their sequence dist.

aisha: Plainsky said avg 30 tokens with occasional 800-token context. Rough mix: 80% short, 20% long.

marco_sec: Security checklist: they require SOC2 section on key management + HSM for secrets. Do they want Private deploy or Dedicated capacity? That changes answers.

aisha: They prefer Redwood Hosted initially, with option to go Dedicated. They're flagged for healthcare-adjacent data, so KMS/HSM need to be covered.

leah_prod: Noted. For hosted we can offer KMS integration via customer KMS token passthrough; HSM requires Dedicated/Private. I'll prepare wording for the questionnaire.

marco_sec: For hosted, we can provide encrypted-at-rest + customer-supplied KMS keys (bring-your-key). Add: we need network isolation clarifications for PHI-like data.

rina_infra: Back to compatibility: can we run a quick micro-benchmark? Suggested testing command for their sample workload:

```bash
# run inference sweep (internal tool)
redwood-bench --model orch-14b-opt --quant int8 --kv-layout compact-kv --seq-dist sample.json --concurrency 8 --streaming true
```

rina_infra: That will surface tail latency and token throughput. I can spin a small harness on Dedicated dev pool if we want reproducible numbers.

tom_se: Also try a run with --kv-layout tiled-kv; some workloads benefit dramatically. We'll need to capture token-per-second and 95th pct latency.

aisha: Timeline: Plainsky demo Friday. Can we commit to test + answer sec Q + a pricing sketch by Thursday EOD?

leah_prod: I can draft the pricing sketch — propose hosted starter POC price with a 2-week discounted block + optional Dedicated uplift. Will share numbers by tomorrow.

marco_sec: I'll draft the security answers today and flag any blockers. If they truly need HSM-backed enclave, that's a Dedicated/Private requirement and a procurement conversation.

rina_infra: I'll run the bench today and post results here. If we see >20% tail latency on 800-token traces we should propose caching strategies and a canary quant variant (orch-14b-opt-qv) to reduce memory.

deploy-bot: Deployment job #7789 started on dev-dedicated-pool (orch-14b-opt v1.2).

rina_infra: bench done (quick pass): 95th latency on short traces ~110ms, on mixed with 800-token spikes 95th jumps to 520ms at concurrency 8. Token throughput drops 18% with tiled-kv vs compact-kv for these traces.

leah_prod: Good data. I'll include the perf caveat in the POC note and suggest two mitigations: 1) enable prefix-KV caching for repeated contexts, 2) offer canary on orch-14b-opt-qv (quantized affine) to reduce memory/latency.

aisha: Sales ask: will quant variant change output quality? Plainsky cares about command accuracy.

tom_se: Small expected regressions for certain numeric outputs; we should run a short eval on their prompt set. If they provide 50 representative prompts we can compare outputs between orch-14b-opt and orch-14b-opt-qv and show diffs.

aisha: I'll ask Plainsky to upload 50 prompts and share access to a sample corpus.

marco_sec: Also flag: their security questionnaire had a checkbox for third-party model audits. We can provide our model onboarding audit summary (last quarter) and list of tested kernels.

leah_prod: I'll attach the audit summary and a recommended sentence for the questionnaire: "Redwood verifies model artifacts with binary checksum, kernel compatibility tests, and reproducible perf benchmarks; for customer-private deployments we can run additional audits on-prem."

aisha: Thanks. Action items recap: @tom_se run compatibility eval + output-diff on their 50 prompts (awaiting prompts); @rina_infra run bench (done) and prepare mitigation checklist; @marco_sec draft sec answers & KMS wording; @leah_prod pricing sketch + audit blurb. Deliver by Thu EOD.

rina_infra: I'll also attach logs and the small harness config after this thread.

tom_se: Once I get prompts I'll run the diff and post a short summary with exact delta rates.

aisha: Plainsky CSM confirmed they'll send prompts by EOD today. I'll ping here when received. :thumbsup:

marco_sec: If they insist on HSM for hosted, escalate to solutions + sales for Dedicated pricing. Otherwise hosted with BYKMS should be fine.

leah_prod: Draft pricing pinned — sharing in a follow-up thread so we don't leak numbers in main channel.

aisha: Great — huge thanks everyone. I'll update Plainsky with a plan and set Friday demo as tentative until we validate quality.

deploy-bot: Deployment job #7789 succeeded (orch-14b-opt v1.2) on dev-dedicated-pool.
